newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HITACHI, ASML DENY BID TALK.
newsitem.headline: HITACHI, ASML DENY BID TALK.

text.p: Dutch semiconductor maker ASM Lithography and Japanese electronic tools maker Hitachi denied on Wednesday that they were in talks on a possible takeover of the Dutch firm.
Shares in ASM Lithography rose five percent or 5.20 guilders to 108.20 on the Amsterdam stock exchange on Wednesday on market rumours of bid interest from Hitachi or Intel of the U.S.

"We don't know anything about it. Both Hitachi and Intel are potential customers of ASML...but don't want to produce their equipment themselves. We are not in talks on that matter," Gerard Verdonschot, ASML Finance Director told Reuters.
A Hitachi spokesman in Tokyo said the Japanese company was not aware of any such plan at all.
Dutch analysts also cast doubts on the market speculation.
"All these rumours nowadays seem to be generated on the floor of the stock exchange itself. It goes with the excitement that prevails in the sector," SNS Securities analyst Bert Siebrand said.
"I don't believe much of it. Intel isn't active in that line of activity...and I don't think Philips would want all wafer-steppers to be produced in Japan," he said.
Philips Electronics NV owns 23.9 percent of ASML.
ASML, a volatile stock which hit a 72.50 guilders low on April 24, reached a life time high of 108.20 guilders today.
